'''Hugo Thienpont''' (born 20 August 1961) is a Belgian engineer.

Thienpont was born on 20 August 1961 in [[Gooik]].<ref name="vubrprofile">{{cite news |title=Hugo Thienpont |url=https://researchportal.vub.be/en/persons/hugo-thienpont |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=Vrije Universiteit Brussel}}</ref><ref name="vubfarewell">{{cite news |title=Hugo Thienpont bids farewell as vice-rector for Innovation and Valorisation |url=https://www.vub.be/en/news/hugo-thienpont-bids-farewell-vice-rector-for-innovation-and-valorisation |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=Vrije Universiteit Brussel |date=4 September 2024}} [https://www.b-phot.org/news/hugo-thienpont-bids-farewell-as-vice-rector-for-innovation-and-valorisation Alternate URL]</ref> He became interested in engineering after watching science fiction media ''[[Star Trek]]'', ''[[Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea]]'' and ''[[UFO (British TV series)|UFO]]'', and decided to pursue the subject in depth at the [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]], despite the initial misgivings of his father Marcel.<ref name="vubfarewell"/> Thienpont earned his bachelor's degree in 1984, completed his doctorate in 1990, then joined the faculty in 1994.<ref name="vubfarewell"/> He was vice-rector of VUB from 2018 to 2024.<ref name="vubfarewell"/> Thienpont is the founding editor in chief of ''[[Journal of Physics: Photonics]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Thienpont |first1=Hugo |title=Welcome to JPhys Photonics |journal=Journal of Physics: Photonics |date=2019 |volume=1 |issue=1 |page=010401 |doi=10.1088/2515-7647/aaf2e3|doi-access=free |bibcode=2019JPhP....1a0401T }}</ref>

Thienpont received the SPIE President's Award in 2005,<ref>{{cite news |title=Hugo Thienpont: The 2021 SPIE Gold Medal |url=https://spie.org/news/hugo-thienpont-2021-spie-gold-medal |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=SPIE |date=14 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Hugo Thienpont wins prestigious SPIE Gold Medal |url=https://www.b-phot.org/news/hugo-thienpont-wins-spie-gold-medal |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=Vrije Universiteit Brussel (B-PHOT) |date=14 January 2021}}</ref> and was elected a fellow of [[SPIE]] in 2006.<ref name="spiefellowvub">{{cite news |title=Nomination of SPIE Fellow for his scientific research contributions in micro-optic and micro-photonics |url=https://researchportal.vub.be/en/prizes/nomination-of-spie-fellow-for-his-scientific-research-contributio |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=Vrije Universiteit Brussel |date=April 2006}}</ref> Between 2009 and 2011, Thienpont served as on SPIE's board of directors.<ref name="2009spiedir">{{cite news |title=SPIE announces newly elected 2009 Officers and Directors |url=https://spie.org/about-spie/press-release-archive/new-board-8-20-08 |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=SPIE |date=20 August 2008}} [https://www.nanotech-now.com/news.cgi?story_id=30430 Alternate URL]</ref> In 2021, Thienpont was awarded the [[SPIE Gold Medal]].<ref name="vubspiegold">{{cite news |title=Hugo Thienpont wins prestigious SPIE Gold Medal Award |url=https://www.vub.be/en/news/hugo-thienpont-wins-prestigious-spie-gold-medal-award |access-date=16 December 2024 |publisher=Vrije Universiteit Brussel |date=14 January 2021}} [https://press.vub.ac.be/hugo-thienpont-wins-prestigious-spie-gold-medal-award  Alternate URL]</ref>
